messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: SLO breach detected for /v1/stream/generate (service=runtime, region=us-west-2). p99 latency 3.8s (> SLO 2.0s). Auto-escalation to on-call. Trace sample ids: trace-9f2a, trace-b3e1.

sanjay: I'm on it. grabbing logs, switching to console. which model is affected?

maria: looks like this started ~15m after the precision-profile rollout to int8-fast for composition-model-v2. metrics show a big tail on streaming responses (stalling at kv-cache warmup). p95 ~1.2s ok, p99 is the problem.

lee: confirming: error budget alert fired at 03:14 UTC. traffic shows roughly 12% of requests saw >2.5s token gaps (stream gaps).

julia: customer-impact check: Support flagged two accounts experiencing partial streams and timeouts (CS ticket 8234, 8240). Not full outage but degraded UX.

kevin: grabbing host-side perf counters. initial read: dequantization CPU spikes on nodes with packed-int8 kernels. Dequant path holding locks while filling KV cache for long-context sessions.

maria: reproduction locally: with long prompts (~8k tokens) and int8-fast profile, we see intermittent stalls when the KV cache hits a slow dequant path. fp16 and fp32 profiles fine.

tara: can we route new streaming traffic to fp8 or fp16 variants and keep int8 for non-streaming? Need quick mitigation.

sanjay: Agreed. Plan A: hot patch routing policy -> prefer fp8/soft-fp32 for /v1/stream/generate for models with sequence_length>2048. Plan B if routing not fast: rollback the precision-profile to previous stable for composition-model-v2.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Rolling update queued for service=router, change=prefer-fp8-streaming, env=prod, started by sanjay. CI checks passed.

lee: I pushed a narrow routing rule to route streaming calls with header X-Req-Context:long to the fp8 variant. Applying to 10% canary now.

julia: 10% canary looks good so far, p99 for canary nodes dropped to 1.9s. non-canary still high.

kevin: while canary ramps, I'm adding a kernel-level guard to avoid holding dequant locks across network IO. This is riskier and needs a short-lived binary patch.

maria: hold on kernel patch unless needed. if router can shift 100% quickly we avoid binary change. How fast can we go to 100%?

lee: if no regressions in the next 5m, I can flip to 100%. telemetry showing improved p99 on canary.

sanjay: flip to 100% now. doing gradual but quick. ops-bot, proceed.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Routing change progress: 10% -> 100% over 2m.

julia: post-flip metrics: cluster-wide p99 dropped from 3.8s -> 1.6s. streaming stall rate down to baseline. customer tickets updated. :thumbsup:

kevin: good catch. I'll keep the dequant lock fix in an internal branch for deeper follow-up. Looks like the int8 profile had an unexpected critical path for long histories that only shows up under streaming (token-by-token) workloads.

maria: note for postmortem: the precision profile decision matrix didn't include streaming token gap tests for >4k contexts. We need an eval harness that tests streaming tail latencies with heavy KV warmup.

tara: customer remediation: offer credits + opt-in to fp8/stable profile until we have a permanent fix. Marketing/CS notified.

sanjay: on-call handoff in 30m. I'll remain available for escalation but handing to lee for the shift. Lee, anything you need at handoff?

lee: I'll own the incident through remediation and the follow-up action items. Please add items: 1) revert-int8-quick-check doc, 2) add streaming-tail tests to CI, 3) kernel dequant race investigation.

julia: adding a monitoring alert to detect similar regressions: create a derived metric "stream-token-gap-p99" on composition-model-v2 for long-context routes.

kevin: also instrument per-kernel latency histograms and expose dequant lock hold time.

maria: immediate next steps: (A) Confirm CS updates and customers on fp8 opt-in (julia). (B) Postmortem draft in #postmortems once incident is stable (sanjay + lee). (C) Keep routing as temporary mitigation until profile is patched or rolled back (lee).

ops-bot: incident-bot: Incident mitigated (status=degraded->stabilized). Root cause suspected: precision profile change (int8-fast) exposed a KV-cache/dequant critical path for streaming long-context workloads. Follow-up assigned.

sanjay: leaving notes in runbook: how to rapidly revert profile for a model id via admin console: nav -> models -> precision -> rollback -> confirm. Saved as quick-revert play.

tara: CS message drafted and sent. Affected customers were offered dedicated fp8 routing and one-on-one engineer support.

lee: handing on-call to julia. I'll be reachable but moving to 1st-oncall for infra.

julia: taking over on-call. thanks team. I'll coordinate the postmortem timeline and follow-ups.

maria: long-term: add a gating rule in the precision-profile rollout process to require streaming-p99 tests and a "long-context KV warmup" eval before promotion to global.

kevin: as follow-up I'll open PRs: kernel-lock-metrics + dequant-fix proposal.

sanjay: closing thread for now. please update the postmortem with timestamps, customer impact numbers, and the exact routing change id.

ops-bot: ticket created: INC-2026-1845. assigned to lee/sanjay/maria.

julia: +1 — will draft postmortem and ping product for severity classification.

maria: thanks everyone. moving to retrospective tasks. :coffee:
